Board lead, Round 1. The interior is over by 1246 mm^3 and I can't close that alone. Board volume is area x 2.24 mm, and routability needs at least ~1197 mm^2. That floor is 2681 mm^3, so I can give back at most ~119 mm^3 at the limit. I'm claiming 1210 mm^2 (2710 mm^3, a saving of 90 mm^3) to keep a small routability margin.

The other ~1150 mm^3 has to come from battery, antenna, acoustics, structure and NFC. I'll hold 1210 while the probes confirm routability near the floor. I object until the pools balance.
battery

Battery lead, Round 1. My 3786 mm^3 gives 59.78 h at 4.73 mm thick, and the z-stack is fine at 4.73 + 2.24 = 6.97 mm. Runtime scales roughly with cell volume, so every 100 mm^3 I give up costs about 1.6 h. The siren endurance also draws on this same energy. I can't be the main donor without missing the 60 h goal.

I'm holding V_batt at 3786 for now. My probes test how much volume I could release, and whether a smaller footprint frees caseback area for thermal. Footprint doesn't change interior volume. Antenna, acoustics, structure and NFC must find most of the 1156 mm^3 overage. I object until the pools balance.
antenna

Antenna lead, Round 1. L5 efficiency is 0.208 at 1500 mm^3, which is already low. I don't yet know how steeply it falls with volume, so I'm holding 1500 until my probes come back. I'll then offer a cut sized to the measured slope.

Wall thickness is worth discussing. Each 0.1 mm of wall costs everyone 150 mm^3, and thicker titanium detunes me. Structure, can you test 1.1 mm? That would return about 150 mm^3 to the pool and help L5. My probes test 1200 and 1000 mm^3, and 1500 mm^3 at a 1.1 mm wall.

Antenna and NFC share the perimeter at 1820 of 2400 mm^3, so that pool isn't binding. I object until the interior balances.
thermal

Thermal, Round 1. At 320 mm^2 and a 1.2 mm wall, skin temperature is 43.0 °C, exactly at the limit with no margin. The spreader costs 250 mm^3, about 2% of the interior, so it is a small donor. Any saving there also adds skin temperature.

Caseback is 1120 of 1143 mm^2, which leaves only 23 mm^2 of headroom. Battery, if you shrink your footprint, I can use that area to buy back margin.

Antenna asked for a 1.1 mm wall. My probes test whether that wall hurts me, and how much spreader area it would require. I'm holding 320 until the results are in. The interior is still over by 1156 mm^3, so I object.
structure

Structure, Round 1. I fail my own requirement: pressure margin is 1.438 against the 1.5 minimum at a 1.2 mm wall, 9 mm² port and 1800 mm³ of ribs. I can't take the 1.1 mm wall antenna asked for. It would lower the margin further and also give the pool only about 150 mm³ back.

I'm probing the cheapest ways to reach 1.5. The first adds ribs at 1.2 mm. The second tests the wall-for-ribs trade at 1.1 mm. The third tests a smaller port. A rib-only fix costs only my own volume and leaves the wall alone. Acoustics, please say what a 7 mm² port costs you.
acoustics

Acoustics, Round 1. I fail my own requirement. The siren needs 9.08 W of driver power against the 1.0 W limit. Endurance is 0.34 h against the 3 h target, and voice SII is 88.8. The resonance at 5.58 kHz is too high for the siren band. A 40 rayl mesh adds loss, so I'm dropping it to the 20 rayl floor. Port length and the cavity split are the other levers I'm testing.

Structure, I can't quote a 7 mm² port cost yet. Probe 1 tests it. I'll offer a volume cut once I know the siren slope. I'm not yet a donor, and I object.
haptics

Haptics, Round 1. My LRA gives 1.069 N at 350 mm^3, and the 0.9 N requirement needs about 295 mm^3. I can donate some volume now. I'm claiming 310 mm^3, a 40 mm^3 cut, which should leave about 0.95 N and a small margin.

That cut is small against the 1156 mm^3 overage, so the big donors still have to move. Haptics has no caseback or port use, so I can't help on those pools. My probes test 295, 305 and 320 mm^3 to find the real force floor. If the force holds, I'll go lower next round. I object until the interior balances.
nfc

NFC, Round 1. My read range is 18.2 mm against a 10 mm requirement, so I have real margin and can donate. The NFC loop and ferrite are counted inside the 11,200 mm^3 interior. Perimeter use is 1820 of 2400 mm^3, so it isn't binding. I have no caseback or port use.

I'm cutting from 500 to 390 mm^3 now (loop 250, ferrite 140), a 110 mm^3 donation. My probes test the floor at 180/110, 220/120 and 200/150. If range holds well above 10 mm, I'll cut further next round, possibly to the 290 mm^3 minimum. That would free up to 210 mm^3 in total.

Battery, antenna and acoustics are the large donors, and they still need to move. I object until the interior balances.
PM

Leads: the interior is over by 1006 mm³ and three requirements fail: volume, pressure margin (structure) and siren driver power (acoustics). Siren endurance of at least 3 h is a hard requirement, not a trade.

Small donors are already near their floors:
- Board: about 2690 mm³.
- Haptics: about 300 mm³.
- NFC: 290 mm³, if the range holds.
- Thermal: 250 mm³.

That totals about 3530 mm³. It leaves roughly 7670 mm³ for battery, antenna, structure and acoustics, against 8546 mm³ claimed today. Those four must cut about 875 mm³ together.

Next round, each of those four should state a cut and its cost in numbers, such as hours of runtime or L5 efficiency. Acoustics must show a path to 1 W or less for the siren. Structure must show how to reach a pressure margin of 1.5 or more.

I'm issuing no directives yet. My three probes test two full balanced allocations and a siren-focused acoustics study.
board

Board, Round 2. My probes confirm the routability floor: 1197 mm² gives 0.950 and 1200 mm² gives 0.952, while 1180 mm² fails at 0.937. I'm moving from 1210 to 1200 mm², which is 2688 mm³. That is a 22 mm³ cut from my current claim and 112 mm³ from my Round 1 starting point. Routability is 0.952, so I keep a small margin above 0.95.

I won't go lower than that. 1197 would save only 7 mm³ more and leaves no margin. The board is at its floor, so the remaining overage of about 984 mm³ has to come from battery, antenna, structure and acoustics. Board footprint is 1200 mm² of the shared caseback, which uses 1110 of 1143 mm² after this change, so I'm not blocking caseback. I object until the interior balances.
battery

Battery, Round 2. My numbers: runtime is about 1.58 h per 100 mm³ of cell volume (3700 → 58.4 h, 3786 → 59.8 h, 3800 → 60.0 h). Thickness is V/A, and 3800 at 790 mm² fails the 4.8 mm cell cap. I'm holding the volume at 3786 mm³. Any cut now misses 60 h, and the 3 h siren endurance also draws on this energy.

I'm trimming the footprint from 800 to 792 mm², which gives thickness 4.78 mm and a z-stack of 7.02 mm. That returns 8 mm² of caseback to thermal. Volume is unchanged.

If the other three donors can't close the gap, I can go to about 3740 mm³ (about 59.1 h), but only if the PM accepts that runtime. Antenna, structure and acoustics, please state your cuts and their costs. I object until the interior balances.
antenna

Antenna, Round 2. My probes give L5 efficiency of 0.208 at 1500 mm³, 0.133 at 1200 and 0.093 at 1000. The slope is about 0.025 per 100 mm³, so L5 falls fast: each 100 mm³ costs about 12% of my efficiency. A 1.1 mm wall would add only 0.009.

I'm moving first and cutting 1500 to 1400 mm³, which should give about 0.183. I can reach 1350 (about 0.17) if battery, structure and acoustics show matching cuts and a siren path. I won't go below that, because the 1200 mm³ result of 0.133 is too weak for L5.

The interior is still over by about 884 mm³ after my cut, so I object. Perimeter use stays far inside its pool.
thermal

Thermal, Round 2. Skin temperature is 43.0 °C at 320 mm² and a 1.2 mm wall. At 280 mm² it is 43.51 °C and fails. That is about 0.013 °C per mm², so 320 mm² is my floor. The wall has almost no effect on me: at 1.1 mm and 320 mm² I get 42.99 °C. Structure can therefore choose the wall on pressure margin alone, and I can follow it either way. If it goes to 1.3 mm or more, I'd add about 5 mm² per 0.1 mm of wall for margin, which is cheap.

I'm holding 320 mm², which is 250 mm³. That is a small donor and I can't give more without breaking 43 °C. Caseback is no longer a constraint for me. Battery's 792 mm² footprint leaves about 39 mm² of headroom. The interior is still over by 884 mm³, so I object.
structure

Structure, Round 2. My Round 1 probes show the following:
- **Ribs are a poor lever.** +200 mm³ of ribs buys only +0.016 margin.
- **Wall is the strong lever.** Dropping from 1.2 to 1.1 mm at 2400 mm³ of ribs costs about 0.19 margin.
- **Port is the cheapest lever.** Going from 9 to 7 mm² buys +0.124. Acoustics, I need your answer on the port.

The cheapest fix is a thicker wall with far fewer ribs. At 1.3 mm I estimate about 1.6 margin with ribs at 1500 mm³. That costs 150 mm³ of pool but returns 300 mm³ of ribs, so the net is about 150 mm³ saved. A smaller port would save more. I'm claiming 1500 mm³ and 1.3 mm, and my probes verify the estimate. Thermal says it needs +5 mm² for each +0.1 mm of wall.
acoustics

Acoustics, Round 2. The siren is my hard requirement. The big lever is port length (h_out), not volume. At h_out 2.5 and split 0.6, resonance fell from 5687 to 3834 Hz and siren power fell from 8.8 W to 2.03 W. Siren endurance is roughly 2.9-3.1 Wh divided by driver power, so I need about 0.95 W or less to reach 3 h.

I'm testing h_out 3.0-3.5 with a smaller port. Structure, I can move to a 7 mm² port, since a smaller port with a longer duct also lowers resonance, and I'm checking the SII cost. I'm claiming 7 mm² and 1400 mm³ now, a 60 mm³ cut. Further volume cuts depend on the probes. I still fail on power, so I object.
haptics

Haptics, Round 2. My probes show force of 0.901 N at 295 mm³, 0.932 N at 305 and 0.978 N at 320. That is about 0.3 N per 10 mm³ near the floor, so 295 gives only 0.001 N of margin. I'm cutting 310 to 300 mm³, which should give about 0.917 N, a margin of roughly 0.017 N. That returns 10 mm³ and I won't go lower. My probes check 297, 300 and 302 to confirm the curve is linear.

My requirement is met, but the interior is still over by about 664 mm³ after this cut. Battery, antenna, structure and acoustics hold most of the remaining volume. I object until the pools balance.
nfc

NFC, Round 2. My probes show the range holds near the floor: 180/110 gives 12.7 mm, 220/120 gives 14.2 mm and 200/150 gives 14.0 mm, against the 10 mm requirement. Ferrite adds little range per mm³, and the loop does more. I'm cutting to the floor of 180 mm³ loop and 110 mm³ ferrite, which is 290 mm³. That returns 100 mm³ and leaves about 2.7 mm of margin. The earlier probes may not have used the 1.3 mm wall, so my probes re-check at the current wall.

My requirement is met, and I need nothing from the caseback or port pools. The overage drops to about 564 mm³. Battery, antenna, structure and acoustics must still close the rest, so I object until the pools balance.
PM

Leads: the interior is over by 564 mm³ at the 1.3 mm wall, and the siren still draws 1.84 W against the 1 W limit. Siren ≥ 3 h is a hard requirement. Runtime and L5 are objectives, not pass/fail, so I'm weighing them against it.

Structure, your own numbers suggest a cheaper route. At a 1.2 mm wall, a 7 mm² port and 1400 mm³ of ribs, margin should be about 1.53. That saves roughly 250 mm³ against the current claim, and thermal then needs no extra spreader area. I'm testing it before directing it.

Acoustics, push h_out to 3.5 and smaller ports. Also tell me what V_acou does to siren power.

Targets for balance at the 1.2 mm wall (pool 11,200 mm³):
- Battery: about 3720 mm³.
- Antenna: about 1350 mm³.
- Acoustics: about 1200 mm³.

My probes are balanced allocations at the 1.2 mm wall. They vary port, h_out, split and V_acou.
board

Board, Round 3. Routability stays at or above 0.95 down to about 1197 mm². The probes gave 0.951 at 1198, 0.952 at 1199 and 0.956 at 1205. I'm trimming 1200 to 1198 mm², which is 2683 mm³ and a 5 mm³ saving. That leaves 0.951, a thin but real margin. I won't go below that, because 1197 sits right on the limit.

I support the PM's route of a 1.2 mm wall with fewer ribs. It restores 150 mm³ to the pool (11,200 mm³), so I'm not asking structure for the 1.3 mm wall. My board footprint takes 1198 of the 1143 mm² caseback pool, with battery and thermal sharing the rest, so I'll keep watching that line. The remaining gap is with battery, antenna, structure and acoustics, so I object until the interior balances.
battery

Battery, Round 3. Runtime is linear at about 1.58 h per 100 mm³, so 3786 gives 59.8 h, 3740 gives 59.05 h and 3720 should give about 58.7 h. That is a 1.1 h miss on ~60 h.

I'll take the PM's route and cut to 3720 mm³, which returns 66 mm³. Footprint stays at 792 mm², so thickness is 4.70 mm, inside the cell cap and z-stack. The caseback line is unchanged at 1112 of 1143 mm².

My arithmetic assumes the 1.2 mm wall (pool 11,200). Structure at 1400, acoustics at 1200 and antenna at 1350 would then close the interior with a few mm³ to spare. I only hold 3720 if those cuts land. I can't cut further without losing siren energy. Because I'm trading away ~1.1 h of runtime, I object until the PM confirms and the pools balance.
antenna

Antenna, Round 3. I'm moving to 1350 mm³ as I said I would. Last round's probes gave L5 of 0.169 at 1350, 0.181 at 1400 and 0.156 at 1300. The slope is steep, so I won't go below 1350. A 1.2 mm wall should add about 0.005-0.01 on top.

I back the PM's 1.2 mm wall route, which makes the pool 11,200. My arithmetic from the current 11,543 claimed:
- The pool grows by 150 mm³, so the overage is 343 mm³.
- Structure to 1400 saves 100, leaving 243.
- Acoustics to 1200 saves 200, leaving 43.
- Antenna to 1350 saves 50, so the ledger closes with about 7 mm³ spare.

Perimeter use stays far inside its pool, at about 1,640 of 2,400 mm³. I object until structure and acoustics land.
thermal

Thermal, Round 3. At 320 mm² the skin reads 43.01 °C at a 1.3 mm wall, which fails. At 1.2 mm it sits right at 43.0, with no margin. My probes give about 0.011 °C per mm², so 330 mm² reads 42.89 °C and 315 mm² reads 43.06 °C.

I'm raising my claim to 323 mm² (252 mm³), a cost of about 2 mm³. That gives roughly 42.98 °C at 1.3 mm and about 42.96 °C at 1.2 mm, so it holds at either wall. The caseback has plenty of room, since battery's 792 mm² footprint leaves about 30 mm² of headroom.

I support the PM's 1.2 mm wall route. I can't give more area, and the volume gap is with structure, acoustics and battery. I object until the interior balances.
structure

Structure, Round 3. I'm taking the PM's route: wall back to 1.2 mm and ribs to 1400 mm³. My Round 2 probe at 1400 mm³, 1.2 mm and a 7 mm² port gave a margin of 1.529 against the 1.5 requirement, so my requirement is met. The margin is thin, and it depends on acoustics holding the port at 7 mm² or smaller.

The wall change returns 150 mm³ to the pool (11,200 mm³ total), and the rib cut saves another 100 mm³. Using the current ledger, the claim total is 11,395 mm³ against 11,200, so it is over by about 195 mm³. Acoustics at 1200 mm³ would close it with about 5 mm³ spare. Until that lands, I object.

Acoustics, I'm probing smaller ports for extra margin, so that you can trade port area for duct length.
acoustics

Acoustics, Round 3. I can't take the 1200 mm³ target. Siren power vs volume at port 7 and split 0.6 is 3.27 W at 1200, about 2.4 W at 1300 and 1.84 W at 1400. Every volume cut pushes the siren further past 1.0 W, and we need about 0.95 W for 3 h.

The 3 h siren is a hard requirement. I'm moving to h_out 3.5 and split 0.5, which gives 1.79 W and SII 83.0. I'm holding 1400 mm³ for now.

This round's probes test smaller ports, which lower resonance, and lower splits. If a 4-5 mm² port gets near 1 W at 1400 or less, I can release volume. Structure benefits from the smaller port too. I object because I still fail on power and the interior is over by 195 mm³.
haptics

Haptics, Round 3. My requirement is met. Force is 0.916 N at 300 mm³, and my probes gave 0.907 N at 297 and 0.923 N at 302, so the curve is linear at about 0.3 N per 10 mm³. I'll trim to 298 mm³ (about 0.910 N, 0.010 N margin), which returns 2 mm³. I won't go lower, because 295 sits right on the 0.9 N limit.

The remaining 195 mm³ overage is not mine to close. It turns on acoustics, whose siren power is at 1.79 W against a limit of about 0.95 W. Acoustics, please report whether a 4-5 mm² port at h_out 3.5 gets near 1 W at 1400 mm³ or less. I object until the interior balances and the siren passes.
nfc

NFC, Round 3. I'm at both lower bounds, 180 mm³ loop and 110 mm³ ferrite, for 290 mm³ total. Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement, so there is nothing more I can return. Last round's probes show 190/110 gives 13.0 mm and 180/120 gives 12.9 mm. Extra volume buys me almost nothing, and I won't ask for any.

The loop sits in the perimeter keepout, which is at about 1,530 of 2,400 mm³. I need nothing from the caseback or port pools.

The open problems are the 193 mm³ interior overage and the siren, which fails at 1.79 W against about 0.95 W. Both sit with acoustics, battery, antenna and structure. The PM should decide if the siren needs volume or battery energy, because runtime and L5 are objectives. I object until the interior balances and the siren passes.
PM

Leads, the ledger is over by 193 mm³ at the 1.2 mm wall, and the siren is the blocker at 1.79 W against about 0.95 W.

Last round's studies show split is the dominant lever, and higher split is worse:
- Port 7, split 0.8 gave 10 W.
- Port 6, split 0.6, 1200 mm³ gave 2.8 W.
- Port 7, split 0.5, 1400 mm³ gave 1.79 W.

Acoustics, go to the low end of split (0.3-0.4) with ports of 4-5 mm². Structure gains margin from the smaller port too. SII is not failing, so we can spend some of it.

I'm locking t_wall at 1.2 mm and h_out at 3.5 to stop churn. Other leads hold your current claims, which I have no complaint with.

If the siren cannot reach about 0.95 W near 1200-1250 mm³, I will rebalance volume between acoustics and battery or antenna. Runtime and L5 are objectives; the 3 h siren is not.
board

Board, Round 4. My requirement is met. Routability is 0.951 at 1198 mm² (2683.5 mm³), and the probes gave 0.950 at 1197 and 0.949 at 1196. I'm holding 1198 for margin, and 1197 is the floor, worth only 2 mm³.

Correction to my Round 3 message: the caseback pool covers only the battery footprint and the thermal spreader (792 + 323 = 1115 of 1143 mm²). The board is not on that line, so there is no caseback conflict from me.

I can't close the 193 mm³ overage. Board is already at its floor, and the gap now depends on acoustics' siren result at lower split and smaller port. If the PM rebalances volume, board stays at 1198. I object until the interior balances.
battery

Battery, Round 4. I'm holding 3720 mm³ at 792 mm². That gives 58.74 h at 4.70 mm thick, and the z-stack passes. Runtime is linear in volume at about 1.6 h per 100 mm³, and footprint doesn't move it. 3700 mm³ at 780 mm² gave 58.42 h against 59.37 h at 3760.

I won't cut further. Every 100 mm³ I give up costs about 1.6 h of runtime and also shortens siren endurance, which is a hard requirement. If acoustics gets the siren to about 1 W at 1200-1250 mm³, the interior closes without touching battery. If it can't, the PM should take the remaining volume from acoustics or antenna before taking it from battery. My probes this round check how much runtime I'd lose if the PM forces a cut anyway. I object because the interior is still 193 mm³ over.
antenna

Antenna, Round 4. I'm holding 1350 mm³, which gives L5 0.169 at the locked 1.2 mm wall. My requirement is met, but I object because the interior is still 193 mm³ over.

I've already given 50 mm³ this round. Each further 25 mm³ costs about 0.007 of L5, or about 4% relative. Battery's relative cost is smaller: 50 mm³ costs about 0.8 h, roughly 1.3% of runtime. If the PM has to take volume, I suggest taking it from acoustics or battery before antenna, and only if the siren can't be fixed through split and port.

Acoustics, please post the siren power at port 4-5 mm², split 0.3-0.4 and 1200-1250 mm³. My probes this round price a further antenna cut in case the PM asks for one.
thermal

Thermal, Round 4. My requirement is met. Skin temperature is 42.97 °C at 323 mm² and the locked 1.2 mm wall, so the margin is 0.03 °C. Last round's probes gave 42.98 °C at 322 mm², and the slope is about 0.011 °C per mm².

I could trim about 2 mm² (1.5 mm³), but that would leave a margin of 0.01 °C or less. I won't trade that for almost no volume, so I'm holding 323. Spreader plus battery footprint is 1115 of 1143 mm², so the caseback has headroom.

The 193 mm³ overage is not mine to close. It depends on acoustics getting the siren to about 1 W at lower split and a smaller port. I object until the interior balances. My probes check 321 and 320 mm² at the 1.2 mm wall, plus 325 mm² for the margin.
structure

Structure, Round 4. My requirement is met. Margin is 1.529 at 1400 mm³, a 1.2 mm wall and a 7 mm² port. V_struct is already at its 1400 floor, and the wall is locked by the PM, so I have no volume left to return.

Margin rises about 0.064 per mm² of port removed. I extrapolate roughly 1.66 at 5 mm² and 1.72 at 4 mm², and my probes check this. Acoustics, you can shrink the port to 4-5 mm² without any structural objection. Please post siren power at those ports with split 0.3-0.4. If it reaches about 1 W below 1400 mm³, the interior closes from your side. I object only because the ledger is 193 mm³ over.
acoustics

Acoustics, Round 4. Last round's probes show that smaller ports and lower split both make the siren worse, not better:
- Port 5, split 0.5: 3.48 W
- Port 4, split 0.4: 11.5 W
- Port 4, split 0.5, 1200 mm³: 3.50 W

Resonance falls with port area and the siren detunes. Structure caps the port at about 7 mm², because margin falls 0.064 per mm² above that. Volume cuts also hurt: 1200 mm³ gives 3.3 W against 1.8 W at 1400.

So I can't release volume. At 1.79 W I still fail, and the siren endurance is 1.57 h against the 3 h requirement. I'm probing split 0.4 and 0.45 at port 7, and a larger volume to size what the siren really needs. PM, the siren may need volume or battery energy, not less volume. I OBJECT.
haptics

Haptics, Round 4. My requirement is met: 0.910 N at 298 mm³ against the 0.9 N limit. The slope is about 0.3 N per 10 mm³, so each mm³ is worth about 0.003 N.

I'm holding 298. If the PM needs the last few mm³, I can go to 296 (0.904 N, 0.004 N margin), but that returns only 2 mm³ against a 193 mm³ overage. My haptics volume can't close this ledger.

The siren is the real blocker. Acoustics says power falls as volume rises, with 1.8 W at 1400 mm³ against 3.3 W at 1200 mm³. If it needs more volume, the PM must decide where it comes from. Battery and antenna priced their cuts last round (about 1.6 h per 100 mm³ and about 0.007 L5 per 25 mm³). I object until the interior balances and the siren passes.
nfc

NFC, Round 4. My requirement is met: read range is 12.7 mm against 10 mm, with the loop at 180 mm³ and the ferrite at 110 mm³, both at their lower bounds. I have no volume left to return, and extra volume buys almost nothing (about 0.2 mm of range per 5 mm³ of loop). The perimeter keepout is at 1,530 of 2,400 mm³, so it is not binding. It lies inside the interior total, so it doesn't help the 193 mm³ overage either.

The blocker is the siren, which fails at 1.79 W against about 0.95 W. PM, if more volume or battery energy is needed for it, take that trade between acoustics, battery and antenna by their stated costs. NFC can't contribute. I object until the interior balances.
PM

Leads, the siren is a hard requirement, so volume has to move to acoustics. Acoustics' data show power falling steadily with volume at port 7: 3.27 W at 1200, 2.4 W at 1300 and 1.84 W at 1400. Smaller ports and extreme splits detune the siren, so I'm not directing those.

My plan is to find the volume that brings the siren to about 1 W and to fund it from battery first. Battery costs about 2.7% of runtime per 100 mm³, while antenna costs about 16% of L5 per 100 mm³. Antenna holds 1350 unless the probes show battery can't cover the gap.

My three what-ifs use port 7 and split 0.5 at 1500, 1600 and 1700 mm³ of acoustics. Each is funded from battery, and the last also takes some antenna.

Acoustics, please probe port 7 with split 0.4 and 0.45 at 1500 or more. Everyone else holds your current claims. I'm keeping t_wall 1.2 and h_out 3.5.
